messages.subject: Using faceting with geom_ribbon
parts:
Dear list,

I'm a bit stuck on a faceting problem:

My dataset looks very much like this one:

df <- data.frame(
x = 1:30,
m0 = runif(n = 30, min = 5, max = 10),
sd0 = runif(n = 30, min = 0, max = 1),
m1 = runif(n = 30, min = 5, max = 10),
sd1 = runif(n = 30, min = 0, max = 1),
m2 = runif(n = 30, min = 5, max = 10),
sd2 = runif(n = 30, min = 0, max = 1)
)

I'm plotting the m* variables vs x (these are mean values of of bigger
dataset for each x), using geom_line.

But I also want to plot a geom_ribbon for each m* variable using their
sd* value (which are standard deviation). I managed to do that on the
same graph:
p1 <- ggplot(data=df) +
geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=m0-sd0, ymax=m0+sd0), fill='red',
color='gray', alpha=I(1/3)) +
geom_line(aes(x=x, y=m0)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=m1-sd1, ymax=m1+sd1), fill='blue',
color='gray', alpha=I(1/3)) +
geom_line(aes(x=x, y=m1)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=m2-sd2, ymax=m2+sd2), fill='green',
color='gray', alpha=I(1/3)) +
geom_line(aes(x=x, y=m2))

The problem is that in real life, the m* variables are very correlated
and thus overlap - as a consequence one can not distinguish clearly on
ribbon from one other. So, I tried faceting the graph.

Here's what I tried:
df_melted <- melt(df, id=c('x','sd0','sd1','sd2'))
p2 <- ggplot(df_melted) +
geom_ribbon(aes(x=x, ymin=value-sd0, ymax=value+sd0)) +
geom_line(aes(x=x, y=value, colour=variable)) +
facet_wrap( ~ variable, nrow=1)

But of course this is not correct as on each facet, the sd0 variable
is used instead to compute the geom_ribbon of sd0, then sd1, then sd2.

Any pointers would be very much appreciated!

Cheers,

Pierre
